Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:150359
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 28296 of 2024

Applicant :- Nanhe Lal Yadav
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Chandan Kumar Jaiswal
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1. Heard Sri Chandan Kumar Jaiswal, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Santosh Kumar Nigam, learned AGA for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 151 of 2022, under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468 IPC, Police Station Sahjanwa, District Gorakhpur during pendency of the trial.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that this is second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and first bail application of the applicant was dismissed by this Court on merit vide order dated 07.04.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 13078 of 2023 and he is pressing the instant second bail application on the ground that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate and in spite of that applicant is in jail since 20.09.2022 i.e. for last almost two years and till date trial of the case could not be concluded.
Nanhe Lal Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66089261/

sentences.text: He further submits that till date even charges could not be framed, therefore, trial of the case is moving with languid pace and there is no hope of its early disposal.
5. He further submits applicant is having criminal history of seven other cases but his entire criminal history has been explained in the instant bail application.

6. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that with a very detailed order the first bail application of the applicant was dismissed but could not dispute the fact that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate and in the present matter applicant is in jail since 20.09.2022 i.e. for last almost two years and till date even charges could not be framed.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. However, it reflects, this is second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and first bail application of the applicant has been dismissed by this Court on merit after considering the entire facts of the case but it reflects that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate and in the present matter applicant is in jail since 20.09.2022 i.e. for last almost two years and till date trial of the case could not be concluded.
9. Further, applicant is having criminal history of seven other cases but his entire criminal history has been explained in the instant bail application.
10. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case including long incarceration of the applicant of about two years, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
11. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant - Nanhe Lal Yadav be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
13. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
